sentences.text: The Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Anna Yojana (PMGKAY) is a welfare scheme initiated by the Government of India.
It was launched in response to the challenges posed by the COVID-19 pandemic.
The objective of the scheme is to provide free food grains to the poor and vulnerable sections of society.
Under this scheme, beneficiaries receive 5 kilograms of food grains per person per month.
The food grains provided include rice and wheat.
The scheme aims to ensure food security for the underprivileged during crises.
Eligibility is primarily based on being a member of the National Food Security Act beneficiary list.
The application process is automatic for those already enrolled under the National Food Security Act.
The scheme was initially announced for a specific duration but has been extended multiple times.
The implementing authority for this scheme is the Ministry of Consumer Affairs Food and Public Distribution.
The scheme is funded by the Government of India.
Additional details include that the scheme also provides for the distribution of pulses and cooking oil in some instances.
